question: Ananga Pala was a ruler of which dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is the__** Rajput Dynasty.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Ananga Pala was a ruler of the Rajput Dynasty, which was a major Indian dynasty that ruled over a vast area of northern and central India from the 7th century to the 12th century AD.**
 
• Ananga Pala was one of the most famous rulers of the **Rajput Dynasty, and he is known for his military prowess and his successful campaigns**** against the neighboring kingdoms.**
 
• Tomar Dynasty:
 
 
• Tomar dynasty is one of the minor early medieval ruling houses of northern India.
 
• Puranic evidence gives its early location in the Himalayan region.
 
• According to bardic tradition, the dynasty was one of the 36 Rajput tribes.
 
• The history of the family spans the period between the reign of Anangpal, who founded the city of Delhi in the 11th century CE, and the incorporation of Delhi within the Chauhan (Chahamana) kingdom in 1164.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The Pallava Dynasty was a South Indian dynasty that ruled over the present-day Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh regions from the 3rd century to the 9th century AD. They were known for their patronage of art, architecture, and literature.
 
• The Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty was a North Indian dynasty that ruled over the present-day Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh regions from the 6th century to the 11th century AD. They were known for their military might and their patronage of Hinduism and Jainism.
 
• The Khalji Dynasty was a Muslim dynasty that ruled over the Delhi Sultanate in North India from the 13th century to the 14th century AD. They were known for their military conquests and their patronage of Persian culture and literature.
